name: Bwile
country: Zambia, Democratic Republic of the Congo
family: Niger-Congo, Volta-Congo, Benue-Congo, Bantoid, Southern, Narrow Bantu, Central, L, Bwile
notes: Bwile is a Bantu language. The orthography uses 'ŋ' for the velar nasal. The digraphs 'sy' and 'ky' appear to represent postalveolar sounds /ʃ/ and /t͡ʃ/ respectively, which is a common convention in neighboring languages of the region. Prenasalized stops (mb, nd, nt, etc.) and labialized/palatalized consonants (mw, fw, ly) are frequent but left as compositional sequences here unless they represent distinct non-compositional phonemes like 'ny' and 'ng'.
